title: 'Bad time to troll': Binance co-founder Zhao asks Musk for support after hack
summary: Binance co-founder Changpeng Zhao asked Elon Musk to stop “trolling” after a $6.3 billion hack, pointing to Binance’s $1 billion-plus SpaceX stake.

title: Kane Parsons believes his interpretation of the backrooms is 'minor cultural shorthand' for the abstract space—just look at South Park's recent episode
summary: You can't pin the backrooms down though, no matter how hard you try.
body: It's always fascinating to see a niche aspect of the internet break containment and make its way into the centre of our collective cultural consciousness. It happened with cottagecore, putting "maxxing" at the end of any word, and it happened with the backrooms, largely thanks to the astronomical success of Kane Parsons' Backrooms film. It didn't take long for brands to jump on the bandwagon and make parodies of Parsons' film. McDonald's dropped its beloved Grimace into the unending maze , Ikea posted themed horror-shorts, hell, even the sponge brand Scrub Daddy posted a backrooms clip . Other than this all being proof that we do indeed live inside a simulation, it's indicative of just how successful this movie was . (Image credit: A24) Parsons' version of the backrooms has become almost "minor cultural shorthand" for all things liminal right now, he said in an interview with Kyle Buchanan . "South Park just did a backrooms episode," Parsons adds. "And you can see already how the version of the backrooms that was presented in the film is overriding and altering the version of the backrooms that existed before this film."
